answer: Sybil resistance arises when trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph: a seed’s probability mass remains concentrated according to conductance, while a sybil cluster linked by sparse external cuts has low conductance. Cheeger-style bounds limit escape and thus cap its aggregate voting weight, even if it contains many jade, shale, and cedar identities; min-cut transitivity prevents repeated attestations from amplifying that bound.
